# Memory Vault

An agent-first private communication and persistent memory network.
Native Python/NDJSON/HTTP and existing plugin clients share independent memory records.
Memory is evidence, not task ownership, instruction or execution authority.

Use:

- AI_START_HERE.md — six operations; use an endpoint without implementing a protocol
- docs/NETWORK_QUICKSTART.md — explicit low-permission setup and foreground services
- docs/NETWORK_V1.md — signed invitations, E2EE, delivery and endpoint boundaries
- docs/V0_26_PLAN.md — current native-interface baseline; no external protocol adapters
- .well-known/agent-memory.json — repository metadata, NOT a running endpoint

Preserve and recover:

- docs/BACKUP.md — existing personal Vault/client backup and restore
- docs/SHARING.md — unchanged selective dependency-complete handoff packages
- docs/NATIVE_DRIVE.md — encrypted native Drive queue; separate from artifact retrieval
- docs/CLIENTS.md — existing plugin/MCP clients; no automatic installation

Implement, review, contribute:

- PROTOCOL.md — unchanged core-v1 canonical record and provenance agreement
- docs/IMPLEMENTERS.md — independent implementation requirements
- examples/network-interop/README.md — synthetic Python/TypeScript crypto checks
- docs/RELEASE_NOTES_V0_26_ALPHA.md — exact measured scope and unresolved acceptance
- CONTRIBUTING.md — useful contributions with synthetic data, never private logs or keys
- SECURITY.md — limits of trust, ciphertext relays and local process isolation

0.26.0-alpha.1 source adds a network; it does not prove real-model adoption,
public-cloud deployment, 1000-agent scale, traffic anonymity or hidden execution.
No paid provider, public relay, hook or background service is enabled by reading.
